extractor.note: Read every paragraph carrying transcend- (outside transcendental) or immanen-, in file order. "Transcendent number" (§35) is the mathematical term and is not recorded. Only the §6 unit carries a stratum, because the commentary marks it as a second-edition footnote; elsewhere it does not separate A from B text.

coverage_note: Term-led pass over the whole file (lines 1-813): every paragraph containing the transcendence family, including bare transcendent and immanent, was read; paragraphs without such a word were not read.

units.claim: The immanent sensation and the transcendent property are not the same item viewed twice: the one is lived through, the other is the correlate of an apprehension of the sensational material.
units.quote: the immanent sensation and the transcendent property are not the same item viewed twice; the one is lived through, the other is the correlate of an apprehension performed on the sensational material

units.claim: The equation of experienced content with experience holds only for the really-immanent constituents, and the transcendent object falls outside it.
units.quote: holds only for the really-immanent constituents; the transcendent object falls outside it

units.claim: In a second-edition footnote Husserl treats the empirical ego as a transcendence of the same dignity as the physical thing, and concludes that a pure ego cannot be evaded.
units.quote: the empirical ego is a transcendence of the same dignity as the physical thing

units.claim: The so-called immanent or mental object, such as the presented god Jupiter, does not belong to the real subsistence of the experience and is in truth not immanent at all.
units.quote: The "immanent," "mental" object therefore does not belong to the descriptive (real) subsistence of the experience; it is thus in truth not immanent or mental at all.

units.claim: The relation is reversed: the truly immanent contents, belonging to the real subsistence of acts, are not intentional but are the act's points of support.
units.quote: then on the other side the truly immanent contents — those belonging to the real subsistence of the intentional experiences — are not intentional

units.claim: Husserl recommends avoiding entirely the idiom of immanent objects in favour of intentional object.
units.quote: it is clear that we do well to avoid entirely this idiom of immanent objects

units.claim: For the distinction between intentional and non-intentional experiences it is indifferent in what sense metaphysically immanent and transcendent being may be opposed.
units.quote: likewise in what sense metaphysically immanent and transcendent being may be opposed

units.claim: Husserl prefers intentional to real for the object because real carries the thought of a thingly transcendence that the reduction to experiential immanence was meant to switch off.
units.quote: carries the thought of a thingly transcendence which the reduction to real (reell) experiential immanence was precisely meant to switch off

units.claim: For really phenomenological consideration the objectivity itself is nothing and is transcendent to the act, which is nevertheless directed at it.
units.quote: For the really phenomenological consideration the objectivity itself is nothing; it is, generally speaking, transcendent to the act.

units.claim: Against the image-theory, all relation of consciousness to its objectivity is enclosed in the phenomenological essence of consciousness, as relation to a transcendent thing.
units.quote: in the phenomenological essence of consciousness itself all relation to its objectivity is enclosed, and can in principle only be enclosed therein — and indeed as relation to a "transcendent" thing

units.claim: It is a grave error to make a real difference between merely immanent or intentional objects and corresponding real and transcendent objects.
units.quote: It is a grave error to make a real (reell) difference at all between the "merely immanent" or "intentional" objects on the one side and the possibly corresponding "real" and "transcendent" objects on the other

units.claim: The intentional object of a presentation is the same as its real, outer object; the transcendent object would not be the object of the presentation were it not its intentional object.
units.quote: The transcendent object would not be the object of this presentation at all if it were not its intentional object.

units.claim: Phenomenological intuition switches off every real existence-positing, including the own empirical ego, and in general everything transcendent to pure consciousness.
units.quote: all positings of psychophysical nature with real things, bodies, human beings, the own empirical ego-subject included, and in general everything transcendent to pure consciousness

absences.expected_because: The pure ego is discussed here, and the second-edition footnote reported under §6 makes the empirical ego a transcendence of the same dignity as the thing.
